items.q: A company buys a powerful CRM service, but the sales team never enters customer data, so the company gets no benefit. What does this illustrate?
o: The provider failed to deliver the agreed outputs
Value depends only on the provider
Value is co-created: consumers must actively participate for value to be realized
items.x: Providers enable value, but consumers must contribute too, by using the service, providing information and adopting new ways of working. Without that participation no value is created.

items.q: The CIO approves funding for a new marketing platform, the head of marketing defines its requirements and is accountable for the results, and the marketing team uses it daily. Which role does the head of marketing perform?
items.x: The customer defines requirements and takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption. The CIO is the sponsor and the marketing team are the users.

items.q:
Which of the following can a service offering include?
1. Goods
2. Access to resources
3. Service actions
4. Governance
items.x: A service offering may include goods (ownership transferred), access to resources (ownership not transferred) and service actions (activities performed by the provider). Governance is a component of the value system.

items.q: A provider delivers new laptops to its customer, which become the customer's property. What is this an example of?
o: Service provision, through the supply of goods
items.x: Service provision includes supplying goods, giving users access to resources, fulfilling service actions and managing service performance. Receiving the goods is part of the consumer's service consumption.

items.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
An [?] is a tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity.
items.x: An output is a deliverable of an activity. An outcome is the result for a stakeholder that one or more outputs enable.

items.q: Which statement about costs and services is CORRECT?
o: A good service removes all costs from the consumer
Costs are only relevant to the provider
The price of a service is the only cost to the consumer
A service removes some costs from the consumer and imposes others, and both must be considered when assessing value
items.x: Consumers assess value by weighing outcomes against costs and risks. Services remove some costs, such as owning hardware, and impose others, such as fees, training and integration.

items.q:
An organization outsources its service desk. Which two are risks REMOVED from the organization?
1. Shortage of skilled service desk agents
2. The provider going out of business
3. Long queues when in-house staff are ill
4. Customer data being shared with a third party
items.x: The provider takes over staffing risks, such as skill shortages and absence. Provider failure and data sharing with a third party are new risks imposed by the service.

items.q: A finance system can process 10,000 transactions per hour during month-end peaks. Which quality does this describe?
items.x: Capacity and performance are warranty aspects, describing how well the system performs. Utility describes what it does, for example posting invoices.

items.q: A user's laptop screen suddenly stops working, so the user cannot work. How should this be classified?
o: As an event that needs no action
items.x: An unplanned interruption to a service, even for a single user, is an incident. The goal is to restore the user's ability to work as quickly as possible.

items.q: Which statement about problems and known errors is CORRECT?
o: A problem becomes a known error once it has been analysed but not yet resolved
A known error is a problem that has been permanently fixed
Known errors are recorded only for hardware
A problem and a known error are unrelated
items.x: A known error is a problem that has been analysed and has not been resolved. It is often documented with a workaround so that incidents can be handled faster until the problem is permanently resolved.

items.q: CPU usage on a server briefly reaches 90% and then returns to normal, with no impact on users. How is this BEST described?
o: As an incident, because a threshold was approached
As an event that may need attention but is not an incident
items.x: An event is any change of state that is significant for managing a service or CI. Not every event is an incident. Only events that cause, or are likely to cause, an interruption or reduction in quality need incident handling.

items.q: Which of the following is MOST typical of a target in an experience level agreement (XLA)?
o: 90% of new employees rate their onboarding experience as easy
All patches are applied within 30 days
items.x: XLA targets focus on experience and outcomes as perceived by people. Technical metrics such as availability and latency are typical of SLAs and remain useful alongside XLAs.

items.q: A team decides what customer data a new service will hold, and how that data will be protected, archived and finally disposed of. Which dimension are these considerations MAINLY part of?
items.x: The information and technology dimension includes the information managed by products and services, and how it is protected, managed, archived and disposed of, as well as the supporting technologies.

items.q: Clear roles and responsibilities, for example documented in a RACI matrix, are MAINLY part of which dimension?
items.x: Roles and responsibilities, organizational structures, culture, and staffing and competencies all belong to the organizations and people dimension.

items.q: Procedures and work instructions that describe who does what and how tasks are performed are MAINLY part of which dimension?
items.x: Processes are often detailed in procedures, which describe who is involved, and in work instructions, which explain how tasks are carried out. These belong to the value streams and processes dimension.

items.q: Which list contains ONLY factors that influence an organization's supplier strategy?
o: Strategic focus, corporate culture, cost concerns
items.x: The factors include strategic focus, corporate culture, resource scarcity, cost concerns, subject matter expertise, external constraints and demand patterns. The other options mix in quality concepts, governance activities and lifecycle activities.

items.q: What is the main difference between the Operate and Deliver activities?
o: Operate identifies opportunities, and Deliver builds solutions
Operate is only for hardware, and Deliver is only for software
Operate keeps the live product running to agreed targets, while Deliver makes products and services available and usable for consumers as agreed
items.x: Version 5 separates running the product (Operate), making it available to and usable by consumers (Deliver), and helping users and restoring service (Support).

items.q: As part of moving to a new platform, the new version is deployed into the live environment and the contract with the previous hosting supplier is ended in a controlled way. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Transition moves new or changed products and services into the live environment, including related arrangements such as onboarding or offboarding suppliers involved in that move.

items.q: In which lifecycle activity are the experience, usability and sustainability requirements of a new product MOST likely to be specified, before the product is built?
items.x: Design turns validated needs into specifications and prototypes. It covers experience, usability, supportability and sustainability as well as functionality and warranty.

items.q: How many activities does the ITIL (Version 5) product and service lifecycle contain?
items.x: There are eight activities: Discover, Design, Acquire, Build, Transition, Operate, Deliver and Support. Six was the number of ITIL 4 value chain activities, five the number of ITIL v3 lifecycle stages, and seven the number of guiding principles.

items.q: 'Include a focus on value in every step of any improvement initiative' is guidance for applying which guiding principle?
items.x: Recommendations for 'focus on value' include knowing consumers, encouraging a value focus among all staff, focusing on value in operations, and including it in every step of improvement initiatives.

items.q: Before redesigning a process, a team analyses existing incident data and also watches agents at work to see what really happens. Which guiding principle is being applied?
items.x: 'Start where you are' recommends assessing the current state objectively, combining measurements with direct observation, before deciding what to keep, change or replace.

items.q: A two-year replacement of an enterprise system is reorganized into a series of smaller releases, each delivering usable value and reviewed with users. Which guiding principle is being applied?
items.x: Even large initiatives should be accomplished iteratively. Smaller, usable increments reduce risk and allow feedback to steer the work.

items.q: A team publishes its improvement roadmap and progress openly on the intranet so that stakeholders can see what is happening and give input. Which guiding principle does this MOST directly support?
items.x: Transparency about work and progress builds trust and engagement, and helps stakeholders contribute. This is the core of 'collaborate and promote visibility'.

items.q: Which guiding principle states that results are delivered through the effective and efficient management and dynamic integration of information, technology, organization, people, practices, partners and agreements?
items.x: 'Think and work holistically' recognizes that outcomes depend on all these elements being coordinated together to provide value.

items.q: 'Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication' is guidance for applying which guiding principle?
items.x: Simple solutions can be harder to design, but they work better and are easier to adopt. This is a recommendation for 'keep it simple and practical'.

items.q: After simplifying the process, a team automates a frequent, repetitive data-entry task and measures the time saved. Which guiding principle is being applied?
items.x: Optimizing and then automating repetitive, high-volume tasks frees people for valuable work. Defining metrics, such as time saved, shows the effect.

items.q: Which statement about governance is CORRECT?
o: Governance is set once and never changes
Governance itself should be subject to continual improvement
Governance applies only to large public companies
Governance is the same as day-to-day management
items.x: Governance must adapt as the organization and its environment change, so governance arrangements should themselves be evaluated and improved.

items.q: An organization plans to introduce AI agents that can take actions on their own. What should governance MOST importantly ensure first?
o: That the AI agents are the cheapest available
That every employee builds their own AI agent
That policies, accountability, human oversight and monitoring are in place for how the agents may be used
That the agents replace the governing body
items.x: Autonomous AI increases risk. Governance should direct its use through policies and clear accountability, define the appropriate human oversight, and monitor behaviour and outcomes.

items.q: Which statement about the continual improvement model is CORRECT?
o: It is an iterative guide, and steps can be revisited when needed
It must be completed once a year by the governing body
Each step may only be performed once
It applies only to technology improvements
items.x: The model is a high-level, iterative guide. Organizations loop back through steps when targets are not met or when circumstances change, and they apply it to all four dimensions.

items.q: When prioritizing ideas in a continual improvement register, what should MAINLY be considered?
o: Which idea was suggested by the most senior person
Which idea requires the newest technology
The expected value or benefit of each idea compared with its cost, effort and risk, and its alignment with the vision
items.x: Improvements should be driven by value. Ideas are assessed and prioritized by expected benefit, cost, effort, risk and alignment with organizational objectives.

items.q: Who can contribute improvement ideas to the organization's continual improvement activities?
o: Only members of the improvement team
Anyone, including staff at all levels, customers, partners and suppliers
items.x: Continual improvement is everyone's responsibility. Ideas can come from staff, customers, partners, suppliers, monitoring data, audits and feedback.

items.q: What is the purpose of the supplier management practice?
o: To establish links with stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performances are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To negotiate the lowest possible price in every contract
items.x: Supplier management covers supplier strategy, contracts, relationships and performance, so that suppliers support quality products and services. It is not only about price.

items.q: What is the purpose of the continual improvement practice?
o: To align the organization's practices and services with changing business needs through the ongoing improvement of products, services and practices
To make sure all projects are delivered on time
To maximize the number of successful changes
items.x: The continual improvement practice keeps practices, products and services aligned with changing needs through ongoing improvement. It uses the continual improvement model and registers.

items.q: Which component of the ITIL value system is a recurring organizational activity, performed at all levels, that keeps performance meeting stakeholders' expectations?
items.x: Continual improvement is a value system component that operates at every level, from strategic to operational, so that the organization keeps adapting to changing needs.

items.q: How does the ITIL value system allow an organization to respond to many different types of demand?
o: By using one fixed process for every type of work
By sending all demand to the governing body
By ignoring demand that does not fit the standard process
By combining lifecycle activities and management practices flexibly into value streams suited to each situation
items.x: The value system is flexible. Activities and practices can be combined into different value streams, for example for restoring service, fulfilling requests or launching features, depending on the demand.

items.q: Which is a key benefit of identifying and mapping value streams?
o: It removes the need for management practices
It guarantees that no incidents will occur
It shows the end-to-end flow of work and who contributes to it, so improvements can focus on what delivers value to consumers
It replaces the need for governance
items.x: Value streams make the end-to-end journey from demand to value visible. This helps teams find waste and bottlenecks and focus improvements on the consumer's outcomes.

items.q: A value stream map shows that a simple request passes through six hand-offs between different teams. What should the team MOST likely consider?
o: Reducing or combining hand-offs to improve flow and reduce delays
Adding more hand-offs to increase control
Ignoring hand-offs because they do not affect lead time
items.x: Each hand-off usually adds waiting time and the risk of errors or information loss. Reducing hand-offs is a common way to improve flow and lead time.

items.q: An AI tool analyses patterns in monitoring and incident data to predict likely failures and recommend preventive actions. Which capability of the ITIL AI Capability Model is MAINLY demonstrated?
items.x: Cognition refers to AI's analytical and reasoning capabilities, such as finding patterns, predicting and supporting decisions. Communication is about interacting with people or systems.

items.q: How does ISO/IEC 27001 relate to ITIL?
o: It specifies requirements for an information security management system and complements ITIL's information security management practice
It is a project management method
It defines the ITIL product and service lifecycle
items.x: ISO/IEC 27001 is a certifiable standard for information security management systems. Organizations can use it alongside ITIL guidance to protect information.
